name: Hold a freestanding handstand
blurb: The genuinely hard one on this list, and the most impressive. Balance is a fingertip skill, and consistent daily practice matters far more than strength.
gear: Floor space and a wall for drills
steps: Own the wall handstand shape first — a straight, hollow-body line held for a minute.
Learn to balance with your fingers: overbalancing is corrected by pressing the fingertips, underbalancing by releasing them slightly and pressing the heel of the hand.
Practise controlled kick-ups aiming to stack rather than to arrive: kick softly and try to catch the balance point.
Do heel pulls and toe pulls at the wall to find the balance point deliberately.
Accumulate practice in short sets — ten attempts of a few seconds, several times a day, beats one long session.
Film yourself weekly; what feels vertical is usually 15 degrees off.
tips: Overkicking is the standard error. Aim to kick to roughly 80% of vertical and press the rest.
Never bail backwards onto your back. Learn the cartwheel exit until it is automatic.
Progress here is not linear. Five seconds becomes twenty quite suddenly, after weeks of nothing.
proof: Ten seconds, freestanding, away from any wall, in a straight line — three attempts out of five.
